claims.exact_statement: Let 0<p<=1/2 (relabel X for p>1/2), theta=arcsin sqrt(p), k(d)=h2(sin^2 d). For every {-1,1}-valued f on any finite product space with interior biases, revealing one coordinate X with P(X=1)=p, with M=H(S_A|S_B), J=I(Z;T) the two terms of the B09 identity L_A=M_A+J_A (bits): (i) J-M <= tau*(p) := h2(p)-m(p), m(p)=min_{0<=d<=theta}[k(d)+k(theta-d)]; (ii) for p<=p0=sin^2(d0)=0.0832217..., d0=0.2926408... the root of cos(2d)ln cot d=1, m(p)=2h2((1-sqrt(1-p))/2) and the two-bit AND 1-2XY with P(Y=1)=q*=1/(2(1+sqrt(1-p))) has J-M=(1-4pq*(1-q*))tau*(p)>=(1-p)tau*(p); (iii) for 0<p<=e^-3, tau*(p)<=(p/2)log2(1/p)+(log2 e-1)p, and tau*(p)=(p/2)log2(1/p)-(1-log2(e)/2)p+O(p^2 log(1/p)). Hence the optimal coefficient of p log2(1/p) in a dimension-free one-bit tax is exactly 1/2.

one revealed coordinate at a time (no multi-bit block claim)

claims.proof_source: Run 20261011T225000Z-claude-B09-sharp-uniform-endpoint-tax: this field and the run StructuredOutput (REPORT.md write was refused by the subagent harness). Step 1: f^(T)=(1-p)g^+p h^, f^(T+X)=sqrt(p(1-p))(h^-g^), q_T=(1-p)g^2+p h^2, sum q_T=1 (Boolean children have unit norm); a_T=(sqrt(1-p)g^,sqrt(p)h^)/sqrt(q_T)=(cos phi_T,sin phi_T); P(Z=1|T)=sin^2 phi_T and, with U the rotation by theta, P(X in S|S_B=T)=sin^2(phi_T-theta); so J-M=h2(p)-sum_T q_T[h2(sin^2 phi_T)+h2(sin^2(phi_T-theta))]. Step 2: h2(sin^2 phi)=k(dist(phi,(pi/2)Z)), k increasing on [0,pi/4]; d1+d2>=theta (same nearest lattice point: triangle inequality; different: >=pi/2-theta>=theta); lowering to d1'+d2'=theta lowers both terms; phi=d in [0,theta] attains; gives (i). Step 3: k''(d)=(4/ln2)(cos2d ln cot d-1), the bracket strictly decreasing, zero at d0; for theta<=d0 k is convex on [0,theta], so the symmetric convex function k(d)+k(theta-d) is minimal at theta/2. Step 4: AND fibers T={} with (1,1-2q), mass 1-4pq(1-q), and T={Y} with angle -pi/2 and bracket h2(p); at q* tan phi_{}=tan(theta/2); (1) gives J-M=q_{} tau*. Step 5: u_i=sin d_i, u1+u2>=sqrt(p); if some u_i>=sqrt(p): bracket>=h2(p)>=(p/2)log2(1/p)+p (p<=1/4); if both<sqrt(p)<=e^-3/2: h2(x)>=x log2(1/x), Psi(u)=u^2 log2(1/u^2) convex (u<=e^-3/2) and increasing (u<=e^-1/2), Jensen gives >=2Psi(sqrt(p)/2)=(p/2)log2(1/p)+p; h2(p)<=p log2(1/p)+p log2 e. Expanding h2(p)-2h2(p/4+p^2/16+O(p^3)) gives the second-order term.
